tools.name: find_trips
tools.description: Finds cheap trips through several cities and countries in Europe or Southeast Asia, strung from non-stop one-way fares, each with how many days ago it was seen: you give a start city (or a home airport outside the region: the trip then starts with a long flight from the nearest big airport we have fares from, which may have stops; each flight says its stops), a window for the first flight, how many places and nights in each, and a flight budget, and optionally the kinds of place (beaches, islands, capitals ...), countries to keep to or skip and cities per country; it picks the cities. Returns the cheapest three trips, each with its flights, fare ages, cabin-bag notes and a link to the trip on faredice.com.

region.description: Where the trip goes. Default europe.

from.description: Start city: a name ("Lisbon") or IATA city code ("LIS"), "anywhere" to start in any of the region's busiest cities, or a country ("anywhere in Germany", "Spain") to start in any of its cities. Needed unless home is given.

home.description: The traveller's home airport when it is outside the region: a town ("Calgary", "London, Ontario") or IATA code ("YYC"). Trips then start with a flight in from the nearest big airport we have fares from (Toronto, New York, Sydney ...), usually with a stop, and from there it's the same trip. The budget covers that flight; getting from home to that airport isn't in the prices. With home, from is used only when we can't fly from that home.

then_region.description: With home: after region, fly on to this other region and home from there, in one trip (europe then southeast-asia, or the reverse). Three long flights: home into region, one across (from or to London or Paris), and home from then_region; each a separate ticket, all in the total and the budget. Homes: Vancouver or Los Angeles, or an airport within 1,000 km of them. The trip always ends home; places_min splits between the regions. A budget of about 2,000 euros fits most.

start.description: Earliest day for the first flight, YYYY-MM-DD. Fares cover about the next 90 days. Default: a week from today.

until.description: Latest day for the first flight, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: two weeks after start.

places_min.description: Fewest places to stay in. Default 4.

places_max.description: Most places to stay in. Default 12, any number.

budget_eur.description: Most to spend on all the flights, in euros, for all the travellers together (up to 5,000 each).

travellers.description: How many adults travel together. Default 1. Every price in the answer, and the budget, is then for all of them.

cabin_bag.description: true: the traveller takes a cabin bag (the wheeled one for the overhead locker), so the budget and the ranking count each flight's usual price for one where we know it; a flight whose bag price we don't know counts €60, the top of the dearest range an airline publishes, so the total is an estimate (see unpriced_cabin_bags). Default true, as the site counts it; false for fares alone.

end.description: home: the last flight returns to the start city (with home, to the airport the trip flew in through). Default anywhere.

finish.description: End the trip in this city, a name or IATA city code ("Rome", "ROM"): its last flight lands there. Not with end home.

must_visit.description: Up to 3 cities every trip goes through: a name or IATA city code each ("Prague"), or {"city": "Prague", "nights": 3, "when": "first"} to pin its nights there (1-14) and when: "first", "last" or a day there, YYYY-MM-DD.

trip_days_min.description: Fewest days from the first flight to the last.

trip_days_max.description: Most days from the first flight to the last.

passports.description: ISO country codes of the traveller's passports ("US", "IN"): countries that need a visa in advance are left out.

kinds_of_place.description: Kinds of place, from our notes on each city: per kind, "only" (every stop is one), "none" (no stop is one) or at least n stops of it (1-4), e.g. {"beaches": 2, "capitals": "none"}. One kind can be "only". Ski counts only from December to mid-April, northern_lights only from mid-September to March, both only in Europe. The start and the return don't count as stops.

countries.description: ISO country codes ("ES", "PT"): every stop is in one of these.

skip_countries.description: ISO country codes to leave out of the trip.

cities_per_country.description: Most cities in any one country. Default 1; 0 for any number (answers write it "any").

held_visas.description: Valid visas the traveller already holds, with passports: "schengen" opens the Schengen area (its days counted against 90 in any 180) and the countries outside it that admit Schengen visa holders; "uk" and "us" open the countries that admit holders of those. The traveller still checks the visa's own dates and entries.

warm_min_c.description: Only places whose typical daytime high for the month of the stay is at least this many °C, from long-term weather station averages (a place without them is left out). For winter sun in Europe.

earliest_departure.description: No flight leaving before this local time, "HH:MM" (e.g. "07:00"), on the hour from 06:00 to 10:00; another time is moved to the next of those (said in notes). A flight whose departure time we don't know is kept, with a note to check it.

latest_arrival.description: No flight landing after this local time, "HH:MM" (e.g. "22:00"; "00:00" or "24:00" for midnight), on the hour from 21:00 to midnight; another time is moved to the one before it (said in notes). A flight whose landing time we don't know is kept, with a note to check it. Long flights into the region are checked by departure only.

visa_free.description: With passports: only countries that need no visa of any kind, leaving out e-visas, ETAs and visas on arrival as well as visas needed before flying.

tools.name: get_trip
tools.description: The trip a FareDice trip link names, as find_trips returns one: its flights with fares, their ages, times where known and cabin-bag notes, nights in each place and the total, with its home hops when it starts from a home airport. food_levels gives each stop country's food price levels as residents pay them, groceries and eating_out, against a typical country in its region at 100 (under 70 is cheap, over 140 dear), from official figures of the year given; tourist areas usually charge more. A trip whose fares have gone says so and gives the nearest days the same places all have fares again, or none.

link.description: A FareDice trip link, as find_trips returns it (https://faredice.com/trip?l=... or /sea/trip?l=...).

tools.name: swap_stop
tools.description: Other places for one stop of a FareDice trip on the same days, keeping the rest of the trip: each with how much the trip's flights change (and its total with a cabin bag, when the link counts one, as its page leads with it) and its link, cheapest first. With city, that change made: the new trip, as get_trip returns it. Places already in the trip, and countries it already visits or (with the link's passports) needs a visa for, are left out.

link.description: A FareDice trip link, as find_trips returns it (https://faredice.com/trip?l=... or /sea/trip?l=...).

stop.description: Which stop to change: 1 is where the first flight lands, 2 the next, and so on.

city.description: A place from the list (its name or IATA city code) to put in that stop's place. Leave it out for the list.

tools.name: edit_trip
tools.description: Change one stop of a FareDice trip and re-chain the rest: night_more or night_less there (the flights after it move a day), night_from_next or night_to_next (a night moved from or to the next stop; the trip's end holds), add_stop (a place after it, with city; without city, the places that fit, each with its change and link) or drop_stop (the stop left out). Returns the new trip as get_trip does, with how much the flights change (and the total with a cabin bag, when the link counts one), how far the end moves and any airport it changes (airports_change). Without change, every change the stop can take, each with its link.

link.description: A FareDice trip link, as find_trips returns it (https://faredice.com/trip?l=... or /sea/trip?l=...).

stop.description: Which stop to change: 1 is where the first flight lands, 2 the next, and so on.

change.description: The change to make. Leave it out for the list of changes this stop can take.

city.description: With add_stop: the place to add (its name or IATA city code), from the list add_stop gives without it.

tools.name: nonstop_fares
tools.description: The cheapest one-way fare seen on each day of the next three months or so from one city to another in Europe or Southeast Asia (non-stop flights), or on a long flight between a big airport outside the region and one of its cities (any stops): each day's price, its age and airline (and, when known, when the flight leaves and lands, local time), the cheapest by month, the airlines with how many days they fly it and their cabin bag rule, the cheapest the other way, and a link to the route's page on faredice.com.

from.description: A city by name ("Berlin", "Krakow", "Saigon") or IATA city code ("BER"). For a long flight, one end can be a big airport outside the region we have fares from (Vancouver, Toronto, New York, Sydney, London for Southeast Asia ...).

to.description: A city by name ("Berlin", "Krakow", "Saigon") or IATA city code ("BER"). For a long flight, one end can be a big airport outside the region we have fares from (Vancouver, Toronto, New York, Sydney, London for Southeast Asia ...).

region.description: europe or southeast-asia. Default: the first region where both places are found, Europe first.

month.description: Only this month's days: YYYY-MM or a month's name ("november"). Default every day we have.

tools.name: nonstop_from
tools.description: Every city one city in Europe or Southeast Asia flies to non-stop over the next three months or so (or that a big airport outside the region flies to, any stops), cheapest first: each with its cheapest fare, the day, its age and airline, how many days have fares and the airlines, and links to each route's page on faredice.com.

from.description: A city by name ("Berlin", "Krakow", "Saigon") or IATA city code ("BER"). For a long flight, one end can be a big airport outside the region we have fares from (Vancouver, Toronto, New York, Sydney, London for Southeast Asia ...).

region.description: europe or southeast-asia. Default: the first region where both places are found, Europe first.

max_results.description: Most cities to list, cheapest first. Default 30.
